title: Segment Anything in Medical Images
grouping: No panels, titles or containers: about fifty square scan tiles in six rows, edge to edge with thin white gaps, cover the whole canvas. Rows run loosely from head and neck scans at the top through chest and abdomen to pelvis, tissue and endoscopy at the bottom, in step with the organs of the body figure laid over the centre.
shapes_depth: Every tile is a real image (CT, MRI, ultrasound, fundus, X-ray, dermoscopy, endoscopy, histology) with its segmentation drawn as a translucent coloured mask overlay, a different colour per tile (orange, cyan, green, purple, yellow, blue). Over the centre sits a large semi-transparent white human silhouette with flat-illustrated coloured organs (brain, airway, lungs, heart, kidneys, gut). No boxes, arrows or text.
proposed_highlight: No model is drawn. The claim is breadth: masks appear on every tile, and the anatomical figure ties the scattered modalities to one body.
lesson: For a 'one model for every task' teaser, tile real scans with their masks as translucent colour overlays, order the rows head to pelvis and lay a translucent anatomical body over the centre, so coverage is the whole message without any diagram.
notes: elements 'other' = the anatomical body illustration. refs crop found no caption (Nature-style 'Fig. 1' with no punctuation), so the figure was cropped by hand from page 3; it is one embedded raster, so photo_share is unknown and the palette is measured over the whole raster. The caption says magenta contours mark expert annotations; at this size only the filled overlays are distinguishable. Venue not verified here (remembered as Nature Communications 2024), so venue = arXiv and year = arXiv preprint year. Annotation note (2026-11-15): Not a method figure: a dataset-coverage teaser mosaic with no model diagram.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: universal medical image segmentation (dataset coverage teaser)

core.what: a mosaic of real scans with translucent coloured segmentation masks, arranged roughly head to pelvis behind a translucent human body silhouette, showing one model's coverage of modalities and organs

relations.form: each tile is a real scan (CT, MRI, ultrasound, fundus, X-ray, dermoscopy, endoscopy, pathology) with its target drawn as a translucent cyan, green, orange, purple or yellow mask
the body illustration over the centre (brain, lungs, heart, kidneys, gut) loosely ties tile rows to body regions: brain scans in the top two rows, chest in the third, abdomen and pelvis lower

channels.colour: mask colour = segmented target, with no key and no consistent mapping across tiles; body organ colours are illustrative
channels.shape: square tiles = individual images; the silhouette = the body

quality.strengths: the breadth claim is carried by real data: dozens of actual scans across many modalities, each with its mask, so the reader sees scope without reading
quality.weaknesses: no method structure is drawn at all (no model, prompt or output relation); the translucent body washes out the central tiles; there are no labels naming modality or target, and the mask colours carry no keyed meaning; the head-to-pelvis order is only approximate

insights.structure: A 6-row grid of real medical image tiles (CT, MRI, ultrasound, fundus, X-ray, dermoscopy, endoscopy, pathology) behind a large translucent anatomical body illustration placed over the centre.
insights.data: Each tile is a real scan with its segmentation mask laid on as a translucent colour overlay (cyan, green, orange, purple).
insights.emphasis: Coverage is the message: the body silhouette over the tiles ties the many modalities and organs to one model, with no diagram or labels at all.
insights.flow: No reading order; the eye scans the grid roughly head (top rows: brain scans) to pelvis and gut (bottom rows).
insights.avoid: The translucent body covers and washes out the central tiles, and there are no labels naming modality or target, so the figure carries no method information.

arrangement.units: one tiled mosaic of image cells with an overlaid illustration; no enclosed method regions
arrangement.inputs_as: real scans with colour mask overlays
